body:
Closes board #112's own follow-up: three more hook-read config gates now honor the same safer-value-wins clamp as `updateMode`, in both Node and PowerShell.

### Security
- `enableConductor`, `disabledCanaries`, and `rotCanaryMode` (+ their legacy aliases `conductor`/`disable`/`mode`) join the merge's safer-value-wins clamp — closing board #112's own next-touch set (board #113). Before this, a project-only `.coalmine.json` could silently re-enable a globally-disabled canary, flip the conductor back on, or re-arm auto-scanning past an explicit global choice.
- `disabledCanaries` clamps by UNION (hooks-safety.md §9: the safer array direction is union, never pick-one-side), not by ordered enum.
- Two escalation holes found auditing the fix, both closed: a legacy key name (e.g. `disable` for `disabledCanaries`) could bypass the new-key clamp entirely; and the merge was storing the raw-cased winning value instead of the canonical enum member, which could silently fail a strict `===` comparison downstream.
- Ported to the PowerShell twin (`ps-config.ps1`), all three keys plus legacy aliases.
- Findings-back: `main`'s CI had been red since `v3.17.0` — the gate-wired PowerShell test suite was still asserting board #112's pre-fix behavior, and nobody caught it locally because `pwsh` is absent on the dev box (the pre-commit gate silently skips it there). Fixed.

Fixes the claude.ai ZIP release-upload race for real — `v3.17.1`'s own claimed fix was unproven, and checking the actual CI run instead of trusting the CHANGELOG entry caught it.

### Fixed
- `v3.17.1`'s "proven live" claim for the Release-upload race was false: that tag's own `claude-ai-zips` run also failed, at the same step, because its `gh release view` probe failed silently (stderr suppressed) even though the Release existed, falling through to `gh release create`, which correctly reported "already exists" and still failed the step. Fixed by removing the `view`-first probe: the step now runs `gh release create` directly and treats "tag already exists" as its one expected success path, erroring loud on anything else.

Per-project config now lives under whichever agent dir a project already uses, not a bare root dotfile — an existing install keeps working with no action required.

### Added
- New read order for `.coalmine.json`: `<project>/.claude/coal/coalmine.json` first, then `.agents`, then `.gemini` (first found wins), then the legacy root dotfile (still read, no breakage). `configure.mjs` and `install.mjs` both write back wherever the config was found — a legacy config migrates to the new location on write; a config found at another new-shape candidate is never force-migrated between agent dirs. The PowerShell fallback hooks still read only the legacy root path this release (named divergence, unchanged).
- The self-update throttle stamp moves to `~/.claude/coal/coalmine/update-check`, with the same read-new/fallback-old + write-new/delete-old migration shape.

**What you need to do:** nothing — an existing install keeps working, and a never-configured project gets the new shape automatically.

Adds a lab-tooling scan-exclude for the session-end auto-scan, and fixes two installer git-hook bugs that could leave the commit gate silently inert.

### Added
- `scanExcludePaths` — a `String[]` config key of path fragments/wildcards excluding throwaway lab tooling (scratch probes, one-shot harnesses) from the touched-files auto-scan, filtered before the scan cap so an exclusion never costs a real file its slot. Global and project layers UNION (a project may only add exclusions, never drop a global one). Matching runs on a linear segment matcher, not a regex, so it carries no ReDoS surface. PowerShell fallback does not implement this key (named divergence).

### Fixed
- The universal installer now honors `core.hooksPath` when writing git hooks — previously hardcoded to `<gitDir>/hooks`, so a repo using husky, lefthook, or a tracked `.githooks/` got a "success" message over a gate git never actually runs.
- A CoalMine hook installed before v2.4.0 is now correctly recognized as ours during install/uninstall, instead of being treated as foreign and backed up/restored incorrectly.

### Changed
- [Developer tooling only — nothing shipped changes.] This repo's own git-hook source moved to the flock-canonical `.githooks/` layout.

body:
The size tripwire now honors a declared over-run instead of flagging every file past 800 lines, and several swallowed-enumeration holes in the gate tooling now fail loud instead of silently passing.

### Added
- The size tripwire (`hooks/rot-canary-touch.js`) no longer flags a source file crossing `tripwireMaxLines` if it carries a top-of-file declaration (`// ponytail: <N> lines at declaration — <why>`, or the existing `waiver:` idiom) — implementing the amended rule that 800 lines is a review signal, not a cap; the finding is an UNDECLARED over-run only. The declaration match is bounded against a measured ReDoS: an unbounded pattern took 5.4s on a poison line reachable at shipped defaults, bounded to ~59ms.

### Fixed
- [Developer tooling only — nothing shipped changes.] Three swallowed-enumeration holes closed in the gate scripts: `manifest.mjs`'s install-manifest walk could silently omit a file from its integrity hash, letting later tamper on that file report falsely clean; `consistency.mjs`'s doctrine-mirror check now fails loud (rather than silently passing) when a rule tree can't be read or enumerated at all, not only when it's absent; and that same check now compares every file in the rule tree instead of a hard-coded 2-file pair list, so a rule outside that pair could previously diverge unnoticed between what Claude and other agents read.

### Changed
- Test files are out of scope for the size tripwire (basename and directory-segment conventions, source files only — a test file's cohesion unit is the module under test, not a line count). The PowerShell fallback twins keep the plain line count (named divergence).

The memory-drift exit-gate advisory (added in v3.12.0) is no longer a loud rot-canary finding — it moves to a quiet, non-blocking channel.

### Changed
- The advisory no longer rides the blocking Stop `reason` that triggers the scan report and fix menu; it now emits on the quiet, model-only `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` channel instead — no severity table, no fix-menu offer, no block of its own. The loud code-scan report is unchanged. The two are decoupled: the scan report keys off files still present at stop time, the drift check keys off whether MEMORY.md was ever touched this session — so a session that edited code, deleted it, and never updated MEMORY.md now surfaces only the quiet note. Detection and guards (the `memoryDriftNudge` off-switch, the root-`MEMORY.md` probe, the `.memmoved` satisfier) are unchanged. On Antigravity the Stop hook still emits the no-op `{}` — no Stop-inject channel there, so the drift note is silent on AG.

rot-canary no longer records or scans files living under `os.tmpdir()`.

### Fixed
- The touch hook records nothing when an edited file resolves to inside `os.tmpdir()` — dogfood-found: a long session's throwaway one-shot harness files live in the scratchpad, which sits inside the OS temp dir, and every stop-scan was nagging on them. The check runs before both the MEMORY.md marker branch and the watched-extension gate, is boundary-safe (a sibling directory that merely prefix-matches the temp path is not wrongly excluded), and is a scan-scope refinement rather than a security boundary.

Hardens the v3.12.0 memory-drift marker write against a TOCTOU race and a symlink-write hazard (CodeQL `js/insecure-temporary-file`, alerts #55/#56).

### Security
- The `.memmoved` marker write is now a single atomic `wx` (create-only) file open, replacing an `existsSync` pre-check plus a plain write — the old sequence had a TOCTOU window and could write through a pre-planted symlink at the marker path. A pre-existing marker (already recorded this session) is now an expected `EEXIST`, swallowed the same as before; a symlink at the path is refused. Behavior is otherwise unchanged.

The rot-canary Stop hook gains a memory-drift exit-gate advisory: a session that edited code but never touched MEMORY.md gets a one-line nudge before it ends.

### Added
- The touch hook records a MEMORY.md edit (any directory, basename match) as a marker, checked before the watched-code-extension gate so a non-code MEMORY.md edit still counts. At session end, if code moved this session and no such marker exists, the Stop hook appends one localized advisory line (all 5 languages) to the existing scan nudge. It fires only when the project already uses the MEMORY.md convention (a read-only existence probe), rides the existing scan nudge rather than firing standalone, and never blocks on its own — the Antigravity Stop hook still emits its existing no-op. Named v1 limitations, not fixed here: a version-bump-only session (no watched code file touched) emits nothing; the check is session-global, not per-repo; it is silenced by rot-canary's own `manual`/`off` modes.
- `memoryDriftNudge` config key (boolean, default `true`) — the standing off-switch for the advisory above.

### Fixed
- `cadence.md` and `escalation.md` freshness stamps refreshed to reflect a re-read against current hook behavior; no content drift found beyond the stamp date.

The installer no longer deletes a directory it does not own before writing to it.

### Fixed
- [HIGH] A no-manifest install used to fall back to hard-coded skill names and delete each one outright — if a name collided with a foreign, unrelated directory, the install destroyed that user's data. The installer now proves ownership before removing anything (the directory is absent, empty, listed in the package manifest, or carries CoalMine's own marker file) and refuses a foreign collision fail-loud instead of deleting it; an owned install still upgrades normally. Found by a CoalBoard audit — the underlying defect spanned three separate delete sites in the installer, not only the one the audit originally named.

body:
Closes a symlink residual left open by v3.11.0's TOCTOU fix on the Antigravity marker write (CodeQL `js/insecure-temporary-file`).

### Security
- `mkdirSync`'s recursive mode silently follows a symlink pre-planted at the marker subdirectory — the directory's `0o700` permission mode is never applied to a pre-existing path, so the earlier atomic-create fix could still write through an attacker-planted symlink into a location outside CoalMine's control. An explicit no-follow check now refuses a symlink at that subdirectory and fails closed (skips the emit) instead. This completes the mitigation v3.11.0 began.

Five more platforms gain hook-configs, Gemini CLI reaches full session-start auto-cadence, file-copy installs get an honest conductor mode, and four CodeQL HIGHs are closed at source.

### Added
- Five new platform hook-configs: GitHub Copilot CLI, Kiro, Augment, Devin CLI (Devin-CLI-only, not Devin Desktop/Cascade), and JetBrains Junie (SessionStart-only — no per-tool events exist there). All five carry the works-with tier; any unverified response channel is marked as such.
- A new `FileCopy` conductor mode for the five platforms above: rule-freshness nudges only — the plugin-update offer and the shared update-check stamp are excluded, both being Claude-Code-plugin machinery, so a file-copy install never consumes the update stamp a co-installed Claude Code depends on.
- `kiro` and `augment` install targets.
- Gemini CLI now reaches full auto-cadence through its genuine `SessionStart` event, emitting Gemini's own nested inject shape (its only SessionStart channel — the flat shape used elsewhere would be silently dropped there). Wired, not yet live-validated.

### Fixed
- Gemini CLI's docs reconciled across five spots — retires a stale "superseded by Antigravity CLI" framing; Gemini CLI remains a business-tier product with its own 11-event hook surface, and only the individual-tier product line ended.
- The Antigravity once-per-session marker write is now an atomic create in a private permission-restricted temp subdirectory, replacing a check-then-write sequence that had a TOCTOU race.
- The stale-marker sweep gained a second pass for the new marker location and now runs before rot-canary's own mode gates — conductor markers are collected on every stop even when rot-canary itself is off or manual; the canary's own temp files stay mode-gated.

### Security
- Closes four CodeQL HIGH alerts (`js/insecure-temporary-file` ×2, `js/file-system-race` ×2) at source.

### Notes
- Supersedes v3.7.9's "the sweep runs only on the active path" note: that was true when written, but the Antigravity port later added conductor markers, a separate class the sweep now also collects on every stop even when rot-canary is off or manual — the canary's own temp files are still mode-gated exactly as v3.7.9 described.

Gate: build + verify + `hooks.test.mjs` 38/38 + `conductor-update.test.mjs`/`consistency.test.mjs` 30/30 PASS.

body:
Two HIGH-severity fixes (a SessionStart ReDoS and a CI test-gate hole), one doc-accuracy MED, and three LOW polish fixes — all reproduced independently by two parallel board audits.

### Fixed
- [HIGH] The SessionStart gold-rule scan was O(n²) on a poisoned rules file — a rules `.md` with many unterminated `<!-- coalmine: verified` openers made each opener's match walk to end of file (measured ~9.2s at 2MB), which could hang session start on a cloned/untrusted repo. Fixed by bounding each opener's match to a 2048-char window, mirroring the same fix already shipped in `consistency.mjs` — linear over the file (~0.47s at 2MB).
- [HIGH] CI's test gate had no missing-file guard — a hardcoded file list passed to `node --test` let a missing test file be silently reinterpreted as a zero-match filter on Node 24, so a renamed or deleted test could drop out of the `main` gate without failing it. A new guarded test runner (`scripts/test.mjs`) now backs CI and both git hooks, so the test list lives in exactly one place.
- [MED] `PRIVACY.md` claimed hooks write only to the OS temp directory and session markers — it did not disclose the conductor's persistent update-check stamp or rot-canary's mode/opt-out file reads under `~/.claude/`. Corrected.
- [LOW] The `disabledCanaries` doc example listed a skill-canary as mechanically disable-able when the key only honors it advisorily for that class — reworded.
- [LOW] `commands/stats.md` said it delivers two sections; it delivers three. Corrected.
- [LOW] A dead sub-expression in the rot-canary merge-conflict tripwire regex, unreachable given an earlier check in the same condition, was removed.

### Notes
- The ReDoS fix and the CI gate hole were both confirmed by independent hermetic timing/reproduction, not by assertion. No `plugin/` runtime capability was added — this is a bug-fix and gate-hardening release.

Token-economy carve to the SKILL.md load path — every canary's behavior is unchanged.

### Changed
- The shared escalation footer (injected into all 9 skills) compressed 27.6% (4170 → 3019 chars per injection, −10,359 resident characters across the suite); the per-platform Heavy-lever table and Heavy-durability prose moved to a new shared on-demand reference, off the Light/auto/Stop-hook path. body:
Ships the config-loss fix to users — earlier post-3.7.3 commits had kept the version number unchanged, so `claude plugin update` never delivered them.

### Fixed
- `.coalmine.json` no longer silently reverts to defaults. The JSONC comment-stripper desynced on a string value ending in a backslash immediately before a later `//` — it leaked escape state, mis-stripped that later comment, `JSON.parse` threw, and the failure was swallowed, silently falling back to all defaults (a config-write path had the same bug and could wipe a user's config). Replaced with one shared, string-aware stripper used by the hook, `configure.mjs`, and `verify.mjs` alike.
- Thai-language text no longer leaks into two skills' `SKILL.md` bodies — removed; skills stay English, and runtime output still mirrors the user's own language.
- The installer now sweeps a retired skill name even with no install manifest present — a pre-manifest install from before the `rotcanary` → `rot-canary` rename could leave the old skill directory behind on upgrade, so an agent reading `.agents/skills` (e.g. Antigravity) kept listing a duplicate command.

### Changed
- Added `CONTRIBUTING.md`; trimmed README/SECURITY for length and heading order; moved the `eval/` benchmark to the series umbrella; restored the "measurement" design principle. SECURITY.md's SkillSpector section now records an actual completed scan run with full provenance, replacing an earlier "binary not executed" note.

body:
A path-traversal guard bypass on Windows in the manifest-integrity check, caught by rot-canary's own auto-scan on the v3.5.0 code the same day it shipped.

### Fixed
- The manifest integrity guard split its keys on `/` only, so a hand-crafted manifest key using Windows backslashes could slip past it — `verify.mjs <target>` would then resolve and hash a file outside the install target (a read-only info-disclosure oracle). Replaced with a resolve-and-contain check that handles forward slashes, backslashes, absolute paths, and drive-relative paths uniformly. Same path-traversal class as an earlier `safeSkillNames` fix, resurfacing the moment new security-relevant code shipped.

body:
Self-consistency + installed-artifact integrity checks land, plus a second, independent eval engine confirms rot-canary's detection quality.

### Added
- A self-consistency layer (`scripts/consistency.mjs`) mechanically cross-checks the artifacts an agent trusts but never verifies: canary-count agreement between `skills/` and `plugin.json`, byte-identical doctrine mirrors across every rule home, and well-formed freshness stamps.
- Installed-artifact integrity: the installer now records a SHA-256 of every file it writes, and `node scripts/verify.mjs <target>` re-hashes the installed tree and flags any file changed or missing since install — a surface git never sees. Path-traversal-guarded.
- gold-standard's RE-VALIDATE pass now flags a memory/decision-log or rule-register entry that contradicts a binding rule or another decision, or names a file/flag/command that no longer exists.
- A second, independent eval engine (Antigravity) ran the rot-canary detection corpus blind: 13/13 recall, 0 false positives on the clean decoys, 12/13 correct severity — the one disagreement sits exactly in the predicted severity-judgment band. README and the eval results now show both engines.
- The Eval harness itself (`eval/`): an AV-Comparatives-style detection-rate measurement — 16 rot-canary fixtures (12 with planted, line-labeled defects across all 7 categories, 4 clean decoys), a mechanical scorer, and model-stamped results. Baseline run: 13/13 recall, 0 false positives on the decoys.
- The Phoenix Commandments (hooks-safety) and scripts-quality doctrine are now published in-repo under `docs/` — the design-principles doc had linked them at a gitignored path nobody on GitHub could open. A repo-wide link audit found no other broken links.
- hooks-safety doctrine gains a Hermetic Hook Testing section (spawn the real hook in a sandboxed environment, assert exit code/silence/state) — proposed by an independent model's doctrine review whose verdicts matched the existing stamps.

### Fixed
- `configure.mjs` now errors on a trailing boolean flag given with no value, instead of silently writing `false`. The eval scorer's confusing no-op exit line was dropped.

body:
The config release — a documented, validated `.coalmine.json` schema, plus a batch of fixes from an issue review.

### Added
- A categorized `.coalmine.json` config system: a 22-key schema in 4 commented groups (interactive behavior, scan and watch limits, re-validation cadences, enterprise paths). The installer drops a fully documented copy at the project root — zero-config defaults for everyone, overrides for anyone who wants them. `configure.mjs` edits it with validation and legacy-key migration; `verify.mjs` type-checks every key; hooks read it dynamically.
- Hooks now resolve `.coalmine.json` from the git root rather than the current directory, so config is honored when the agent works from a subdirectory. The installer supports worktree/submodule `.git` files and refuses to target CoalMine's own source `skills/` directory.
- An auto-scan token cap: past a configured file count, only the most recently touched files are scanned, with a localized notice appended (all 5 languages).

### Fixed
- Touched files are now recorded as absolute paths in both the Node and PowerShell touch hooks — a subdirectory edit no longer vanishes from the stop-hook scan.
- The temp-sweep cadence is now deterministic: a 24-hour marker-file gate replaces a randomized-probability throttle, in both Node and PowerShell; the PowerShell sweep also clears legacy marker files from a prior naming scheme.
- Legacy v3.0.0 config key names work again alongside the current names, in all five hooks; the README schema table no longer contradicts the canonical keys.
- Hook stdin is now BOM-hardened — some shells prepend a byte-order mark when piping JSON, which previously broke parsing.
- Config is now read once per hook invocation instead of 4-5 times with a git-root walk each time.
- Skill docs conform to one canonical structure (Fix mode before Output, one consistent heading name), and `/coalmine:stats` again advises `claude plugin update`.
